crumb the parent `bx-breadcrumb` can navigate via a click handler without a real URL, e.g. SPA
routing); `current` set → plain text with `aria-current="page"` (docs/features/core/breadcrumb-
item.md §6's "aria-current on last" — `current` isn't in the spec's own properties table but is
how the not-yet-built `bx-breadcrumb` parent would mark the last item, per §10's "confirm final
property names during implementation").

declarations.name: BxBreadcrumb
declarations.description:
`<bx-breadcrumb>` — navigation trail owning a default-slotted set of `bx-breadcrumb-item`
(docs/features/core/breadcrumb.md).

Sets `role="listitem"` on each slotted item (the spec's §6 "ordered list semantics" — items
themselves don't render as `<li>`, so this element supplies that role rather than requiring
every item author to remember it) and drives `current` on the last one (FR-BREADCRUMB-02);
`bx-breadcrumb-item`'s own `:host(:last-child)` CSS already hides a trailing separator on
whichever item ends up last in DOM order, so hiding items for overflow (below) doesn't need any
extra separator bookkeeping.

FR-BREADCRUMB-01's "ellipsis dropdown" is implemented as an inline expand rather than a floating
popover menu: clicking "…" un-hides the collapsed items in place. A `bx-popup`-anchored menu
would need a lightweight menu-list primitive this package doesn't have yet (`bx-dropdown` is
Tier 4, `VirtualizerController`-gated) — noted here per docs/features/_conventions.md's "say so
inline" rule rather than pulled in over-scope for a Tier 2 component. Collapse math measures
each item's natural (unhidden) width once per resize/slot-change and hides from the earliest
middle item outward until the remainder fits, the same single-measurement-pass approach
`bx-scroller`'s edge shadows and `bx-tab-group`'s scroll buttons already use.

declarations.name: BxButtonGroup
declarations.description:
`<bx-button-group>` — groups related buttons into a single segmented control with shared borders
(docs/features/core/button-group.md).

Children keep their own identity and behavior — the group only lays them out and squares their
inner corners. The corners are shaped through `bx-button`'s public `--bx-button-radius` custom
property (set on each slotted item via `::slotted`, and inherited on into wrappers such as
`bx-copy-button`), not by reaching into any child's shadow root, so any component that ends in a
`bx-button` composes (FR-BUTTON-GROUP-01). A `bx-tooltip` wrapped item is made a real box
(`display: inline-flex`, overriding its `display: contents`) so it can take part in the seams and
the hover/focus raise. RTL flips the outer-corner rounding via `:dir(rtl)`.

Seams collapse by pulling every item after the first back by one border width; `--bx-button-group-gap`
overrides that offset (set a positive length for a spaced-out group). A hovered or focused item is
raised above its neighbors (FR-BUTTON-GROUP-03) so its border and focus ring are not clipped.

`variant` and `size`, when set, are applied to every descendant `bx-button` and `bx-copy-button` (FR-BUTTON-GROUP
property table: "optionally forces variant/size on children"). Unset, each button keeps its own.

Not implemented from the spec, flagged inline per docs/features/_conventions.md: FR-BUTTON-GROUP-04's
`overflow="menu"` (needs `bx-dropdown`, Tier 4), the `stack-narrow` container-query stacking and
the `toolbar` roving-arrow-key mode. Each button stays in the tab order, which is the default
behavior §6 asks for.

declarations.name: BxButton
declarations.description:
`<bx-button>` — triggers an action, navigates (link mode), or submits/resets a form
(docs/features/core/button.md).

Renders a real inner `<button>` or, when `href` is set, a real inner `<a>` — native
activation, focus and (for links) Ctrl/Cmd-click/middle-click/`download` semantics come free
(FR-BUTTON-02), no reimplementation needed. The spec's own header table says
"Form-associated: No" while FR-BUTTON-01 asks for submit/reset to "act on the associated form
via ElementInternals" — those two lines don't actually agree. This resolves the tension the
simpler way: a trigger button carries no value, so it doesn't need `FormAssociatedMixin`'s
`setFormValue`/validity plumbing (matching "No"); it only needs to find the right `<form>`
(`form` attribute → `getElementById`, else the nearest ancestor `<form>`) and call
`requestSubmit()`/`reset()` on it directly (satisfying FR-01's actual functional ask).

FR-BUTTON-06 ("disabled must not swallow events silently in a way that breaks tooltips") is why
`disabled` is never rendered as the inner control's native `disabled` attribute — a native
`disabled` control suppresses pointer events entirely, which would make a future `bx-tooltip`
anchored to a disabled button impossible to show on hover. Instead the inner control stays
focusable and hoverable, gets `aria-disabled`, and every activation path
(click/Enter/Space/`requestSubmit`) is guarded in script.

`--bx-button-truncate` (FR-BUTTON-05) is the literal `white-space` value applied to the label:
unset, it falls back to `normal` (wraps, the spec's default); set it to `nowrap` to truncate
with an ellipsis instead.

`target`/`rel`/`download` aren't in the spec's own properties table but are required for
FR-BUTTON-02's link-mode behavior — added the same way `bx-radio`'s `name`/`checked` fill an
analogous gap in that component's own spec.

`aria-label`/`aria-labelledby` set on the host are forwarded onto the inner `<button>`/`<a>`
in `updated()` (`aria-labelledby` via `ariaLabelledByElements`, the same cross-shadow-root
element-reference reflection `bx-tab-group` uses): the host itself isn't the accessible,
interactive element, so those attributes have no effect left where an author would naturally
put them otherwise — FR-BUTTON-04's icon-only case is exactly this.

declarations.name: BxCarouselItem
declarations.description:
`<bx-carousel-item>` — a single slide.

Deliberately stateless (FR-CAROUSEL-ITEM-01): no index/position tracking, no snap logic of its
own. Scroll-snap alignment is declared by the parent `bx-carousel` through the
`--bx-carousel-item-snap-align` custom property rather than a hardcoded `scroll-snap-align` — an
item with no carousel parent (e.g. rendered standalone in a test or story) still lays out
correctly, it just doesn't snap.

`role="group"` and its position label (docs/features/core/carousel-item.md §6) go on the host
itself, the same host-attribute pattern `bx-divider` uses — there are no interactive parts or
slots to hang them on, and the spec lists no CSS parts for this component.

declarations.name: BxCarousel
declarations.description:
`<bx-carousel>` — scroll-snap carousel with pagination, navigation, autoplay and drag.

CSS scroll-snap does the actual layout and momentum (FR-CAROUSEL-01): the scroll container is a
plain `overflow: auto` flexbox with `scroll-snap-type`, so touch/trackpad scrolling, momentum and
accessibility all come from the platform for free. JS only tracks which slide is current (via a
shared `IntersectionObserver` on each slide), drives `next()`/`previous()`/`goToSlide()` through
`scrollIntoView()`, and wires up navigation buttons, pagination dots and autoplay.

Slides are `<bx-carousel-item>` children; this component sets each one's `label` ("n of m") and
`--bx-carousel-item-snap-align` per that component's contract — it is deliberately stateless on
its own (see its own docstring).

Autoplay pauses on hover, focus-within, a hidden tab and `prefers-reduced-motion`
(FR-CAROUSEL-02); a pause/play control lives next to the navigation for keyboard/AT users
regardless of hover/focus state (docs/features/core/carousel.md §6).

`slides-per-page` accepts a single number or a container-width-keyed map
(`"1 480px:2 800px:3"`, FR-CAROUSEL-04); the count is re-resolved on host resize.

declarations.name: BxCheckbox
declarations.description:
`<bx-checkbox>` — binary or indeterminate selection, form-associated via `ElementInternals`.

inherited `focus()`/`blur()`/`click()` (the spec's public methods, docs/features/core/checkbox.md
§2) work without any override: `delegatesFocus` sends `host.focus()` to the control, and a
single host-level click/keydown listener catches synthetic `host.click()`, real clicks on
slotted light-DOM label text, and clicks on the shadow control itself (all composed-bubble to
the host either way).

FR-CHECKBOX-05's "lite" render path for `bx-data-table` row selection is deferred until that
package exists to define what "lite" needs to skip — nothing here depends on it yet.

declarations.name: BxColorPicker
declarations.description:
`<bx-color-picker>` — color selection with a saturation/value grid, hue/alpha sliders,
swatches, eyedropper and format switching, form-associated via `ElementInternals`
(docs/features/core/color-picker.md).

The canonical internal state is HSV + alpha (`Hsva`), not the `format`-displayed string: the
saturation/value grid maps directly to `s`/`v`, and every other representation (hex/rgb/hsl) is
a pure, lossless-enough derivation from it (FR-COLOR-PICKER-06) computed on demand, not stored.
`value` (the form value and `getFormattedValue()`'s default) is that derivation in the current
`format`.

FR-COLOR-PICKER-05's rAF-coalescing applies to the grid and slider `pointermove` handlers
specifically (dragging can fire many events per frame); clicks, keyboard steps and the text
input commit immediately, since there's nothing to coalesce there.

Non-`inline` mode reuses `bx-popup` for the trigger→panel relationship, with click-outside and
Escape dismissal — the same pattern `bx-tooltip` wires up for its own `bx-popup`, plus the
outside-click handling a hover-driven tooltip never needed. `open` isn't in the spec's own
properties table but is required for this non-`inline` mode to have any state to toggle at all;
added the same way other components fill an analogous gap in their own specs.

declarations.name: BxCopyButton
declarations.description:
`<bx-copy-button>` — one-click copy of text, a property, or another element's content to the
clipboard, with success/error feedback (docs/features/core/copy-button.md).

A composite of existing pieces rather than a bespoke control: a `bx-button` (plain appearance,
icon-only) anchors a `bx-tooltip` whose text is the current label — the copy prompt at rest, then
the success/error message for `feedback-duration` after an attempt. The icons are `bx-icon`s
(`copy`, `check`, `warning`) behind slots, so anything slotted replaces them. Because it is a
real `bx-button`, `disabled`, focus ring, hit-target size and forced-colors handling are all
inherited, and `bx-button-group` can square its corners (`--bx-button-radius` inherits into it).

The accessible name is the current label (FR-COPY-BUTTON accessibility): it is forwarded onto the
inner button as `aria-label`, and each state change is announced through a visually hidden
polite live region (FR-COPY-BUTTON-03) — the tooltip alone is not exposed to assistive tech.

The success/error colors default to the design system's success/danger role tokens; the spec's
`--bx-success-color`/`--bx-error-color` are prefixed with the component name here
(`--bx-copy-button-success-color`) to follow the package's custom-property naming rule.

declarations.name: BxDetails
declarations.description:
`<bx-details>` — disclosure widget; supports grouping into an accordion via `name`.

The header is a real `<button>` (native keyboard/focus semantics for free) with
`aria-expanded`/`aria-controls` on it, per the disclosure pattern (docs/features/core/details.md
§6). The body's open/close animation (FR-DETAILS-01) measures the content's natural height in
JS and transitions `block-size` to/from it explicitly (see `updated()`), rather than the
"grid-template-rows: minmax(0, Nfr)" auto-height trick this used to use: that technique
requires the browser to compute an intrinsic max-content contribution through a `<slot>` for
the `fr` track, and empirically, in this project's pinned Chromium, the close direction
(1fr -> 0fr) would sometimes never transition at all — the row just stayed at its open size,
no animation running, only the open direction reliably worked. Independent show/hide durations
still come from the same place (the base rule and the `[open]` rule each carry their own
`transition-duration`); only the *value* being transitioned changed.

With `lazy`, the default slot's content is not rendered until the details is opened for the
first time, deferring heavy children (FR-DETAILS-02) — note this needs an actual `lazy`
attribute even though it isn't listed in the spec's own properties table; see §10's "confirm
final property names during implementation".

declarations.name: BxDialog
declarations.description:
`<bx-dialog>` — modal dialog built on native `<dialog>`, with header, footer and light dismiss.

`showModal()`/`close()` on the native element provide the inert background, focus trap and
top-layer stacking for free (FR-DIALOG-01) — this component only adds the header/footer
chrome, light-dismiss, `data-dialog="close"` delegation and focus-return bookkeeping on top.

The default close button is a real `<bx-button>` (styled via `::part(base)` into its round
icon-button shape) rather than a bespoke `<button>` — this makes `bx-dialog` a Tier 1 component
that depends on a Tier 2 one (docs/features/IMPLEMENTATION.md), a deliberate exception to the
usual build-order layering now that `bx-button` exists, so every dialog's close control gets
`bx-button`'s own disabled/hover/focus/forced-colors handling for free instead of a second,
separately-maintained implementation of the same thing.

Sizing intentionally uses `vi` (viewport-inline), not a container query: a top-layer element has
no ancestor that provides an `inline-size` containment context to query against — its size
decision is inherently relative to the viewport, which is the one legitimate exception to
"container queries, never media queries" (docs/features/_conventions.md §3); see also
`scroller.md`'s documented fallback-path exception for the same kind of API-availability gap.

declarations.name: BxDrawer
declarations.description:
`<bx-drawer>` — edge-anchored panel (top/end/bottom/start), modal or contained to a parent
(docs/features/core/drawer.md).

Same dialog semantics as `bx-dialog` (FR-DRAWER, §6): a native `<dialog>`, so the default modal
mode gets the inert background, focus trap and top-layer stacking from `showModal()`. The
header chrome (title slot, header-actions, close `bx-button`), light-dismiss, `data-drawer="close"`
delegation, cancelable `bx-hide` with `detail.source` and focus return all mirror `bx-dialog`
— kept as a parallel implementation rather than a shared base since the two only overlap in
that bookkeeping, not in layout, and a base class would be the first abstraction extracted from
exactly two users.

`contained` opens the native dialog non-modally (`show()`) instead, and positions it inside the
nearest positioned ancestor rather than the viewport: the drawer's host fills that ancestor
(`position: absolute; inset: 0`), so **the parent must establish a containing block**
(`position: relative`). A rendered `overlay` scrim sits behind the panel and, without a trap,
focus is free to leave — FR-DRAWER-02's "do not trap focus outside their parent". Escape is
handled by a keydown listener since a non-modal `<dialog>` doesn't receive the native `cancel`.

Placements use logical insets (RTL-aware `start`/`end`, FR-DRAWER-03); the slide-in animates
`transform` only and is disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion` (FR-DRAWER-01). Size uses `vi`
in modal mode for the same top-layer reason `bx-dialog` does, and clamps to the container so it
fills narrow ones (§5). There is no close animation, matching `bx-dialog`.

declarations.name: BxDropdownItem
declarations.description:
`<bx-dropdown-item>` — a single menu entry: plain, checkbox, radio, or submenu parent.

`role`/`aria-haspopup` are set from this element's own state (`type`, whether the `submenu`
slot has assigned content) rather than by a parent, so it is correct standalone.
FR-DROPDOWN-ITEM-02's `focusable-disabled` is read from the nearest ancestor carrying that
attribute via `closest()` so `bx-dropdown` only has to set it once on itself.

**Submenus (FR-DROPDOWN-03).** A `submenu` slot with children turns the item into a submenu
parent: the nested items render in an internal `bx-popup` beside the row. It opens on hover
(after a short dwell), on `ArrowRight` (`ArrowLeft` in RTL), and on Enter/Space; `ArrowLeft`/
`Escape` close it and return focus to the parent. Hover uses a safe triangle — while the pointer
crosses sibling rows on its way to the submenu it stays open. Activating a submenu parent opens
it instead of firing `bx-select`. Only one submenu per menu is open at a time.

**Additions beyond the spec's tables** (flagged per docs/features/_conventions.md): `type="radio"`
with a `name` makes `menuitemradio` items that deselect same-`name` siblings (FR-DROPDOWN-04's
"radio-like groups"); `submenu-open`; `set-size`/`pos-in-set` for windowed menus, which cannot
rely on DOM siblings for `aria-setsize`/`aria-posinset`; a `submenu` CSS part; `focus()`
delegates to the row. The host no longer carries `container-type` — it made every fixed-position
descendant (the submenu popup) resolve against the row instead of the viewport — so the
"details hide when narrow" container query now measures the inner row.

declarations.name: BxDropdown
declarations.description:
`<bx-dropdown>` — anchors a menu of `bx-dropdown-item`s to a trigger, positioned by an internal
`bx-popup` (flip, shift, available-height sizing). Keyboard navigable (arrows with wrap,
Home/End, typeahead, Escape returns focus to the trigger), with checkbox, radio and nested
submenu items (docs/features/core/dropdown.md).

**Focus model.** Real DOM focus moves onto the items (roving, programmatic) as the menu pattern
in the ARIA APG describes; the trigger gets `aria-haspopup="menu"`/`aria-expanded` and the
menu is `aria-labelledby` the trigger. Tab closes the menu and lets focus continue from the
trigger; outside clicks and focus leaving close it.

**Two ways to supply items.** Slotted `bx-dropdown-item`/`bx-divider` children (the default), or
the `items` data array. Only the data path can be virtualized (FR-DROPDOWN-05): with `virtual`
set and more than `virtual-threshold` entries, just the rows in the visible window exist in the
DOM, the row holding focus is pinned so scrolling never drops it, and typeahead, Home/End and
`aria-setsize`/`aria-posinset` all run over the full array. Slotted children cannot be
windowed — they are the consumer's elements — so `virtual` has no effect on them. Data items
are flat (no submenus), and their `checked` state is held by the dropdown so it survives node
recycling; assign a new `items` array to reset it.

**Deviations / gaps, per docs/features/_conventions.md's "say so inline" rule:**
- The `items` property, `focusable-disabled` (FR-DROPDOWN-ITEM-02, read by the items through
  `closest()`), `type="radio"` items and the `reserve checkmark` handling for data rows are
  additions to the spec's tables.
- §5's narrow-container bottom sheet (`sheet-narrow`) is not implemented; the menu is always a
  popup that flips and shifts to stay in the viewport.
- The trigger is expected to be a button-like control (`bx-button`, `<button>`): Enter/Space
  activate it through its own click, so they are not re-handled here.

declarations.name: BxFormatBytes
declarations.description:
`<bx-format-bytes>` — formats a byte/bit count in a locale-aware, human-readable form.

Picks the largest unit that keeps the magnitude under the base (1024 for bytes, 1000 for bits)
and formats it through `Intl.NumberFormat`'s `unit` style, so "1536" renders as "1.5 kB" rather
than a raw byte count (FR-FORMAT-BYTES-01). Formatters are cached per (locale, unit, display) —
see `internal/intl-cache.ts` — since instantiating `Intl.NumberFormat` repeatedly is expensive
and this component is meant to appear many times (e.g. one per row in a file list).

declarations.name: BxFormatDate
declarations.description:
`<bx-format-date>` — formats a date via `Intl.DateTimeFormat`.

`date` accepts a `Date` (set as a JS property) or an ISO-parseable string (attribute or
property); omitted, it formats the current time at each render, matching the spec's "now"
default. The remaining attributes mirror `Intl.DateTimeFormat` option names 1:1 (`hour-format`
maps to `hourCycle`) so callers already familiar with the `Intl` API need no translation table.
Formatters are cached per option set (`internal/intl-cache.ts`, FR-FORMAT-DATE-01).

An unparseable `date` renders nothing and logs a console warning rather than throwing or
showing "Invalid Date" (FR-FORMAT-DATE-01).

declarations.name: BxFormatNumber
declarations.description:
`<bx-format-number>` — formats numbers, currency and percent via `Intl.NumberFormat`.

Renders straight into light DOM (`createRenderRoot` returns `this`) instead of the usual shadow
root: FR-FORMAT-NUMBER-02 calls this out explicitly because this element is meant to appear by
the thousand in `bx-data-table`/`bx-data-list` cells, where a shadow root per instance is
measurable overhead for a component that is, in the end, one text node. That also means there
are no `::part()`/slot hooks — style it like any other inline text via the host's own `style`/
`class`, same as a `<span>`.

Formatters are cached per option set (`internal/intl-cache.ts`) and that cache is shared with
the future `bx-number-input` (FR-FORMAT-NUMBER-01), so the two never construct redundant
`Intl.NumberFormat` instances for the same shape.

Resolves either `src` (fetched directly) or `name`/`library`/`family`/`variant` against a
library registered with ; the bundled `default` library needs no
network. Results are sanitised (`<script>`/`<foreignObject>` stripped), cached and de-duplicated

declarations.name: BxOption
declarations.description:
`<bx-option>` — a single item inside `bx-select`.

Deliberately inert (FR-OPTION-01): it owns no selection logic and attaches no listeners of its
own — `value`/`label`/`selected`/`disabled` are plain reflected properties that a parent list
(`bx-select`) reads and writes directly, the same way native `<option>` is a dumb data holder
for `<select>`. That parent is also responsible for focus management (`aria-activedescendant`)
per the APG listbox pattern; this element does not set `tabindex` itself.

`role="option"`, `aria-selected` and `aria-disabled` live on the *host*, not on an element in
the shadow root: a combobox's `aria-activedescendant` has to point at the element that carries
the role, and an ID reference cannot reach into another element's shadow tree. The host
attributes are only written when the consumer has not set them, so an explicit `role` wins.
A parent that virtualizes sets `aria-setsize`/`aria-posinset` on the host directly. `data-active`
(set by the parent) paints the keyboard/hover highlight.

declarations.name: BxPage
declarations.description:
`<bx-page>` — application shell: banner, header, subheader, navigation, main, aside and footer
regions with a responsive collapse (docs/features/core/page.md).

**View switching (FR-PAGE-01).** `view` is derived from the *page element's own inline size*
(shared `ResizeObserver`), not the viewport, so the shell works when embedded in a
micro-frontend. A CSS container query cannot take a configurable threshold, so the measured
value is reflected as `view="mobile|desktop"` and the stylesheet keys off that attribute.
`mobile-breakpoint` accepts any CSS length (`48rem`, `60em`, `600px`); it is resolved to pixels
through a probe element so relative units follow the root font size.

**Off-canvas navigation (FR-PAGE-02).** In the mobile view the navigation is a drawer inside
the page (absolutely positioned, so it stays within the embedding container). Opening it moves
focus into the navigation and makes everything else `inert`; Escape, the scrim or the hide
button close it and focus returns to the menu button. In the desktop view it is a permanent
column and `nav-open` has no effect.

**Landmarks (FR-PAGE-03).** `header` (banner), `nav`, `main`, `aside` (complementary) and
`footer` (contentinfo) are real landmark elements in the shadow root; the skip link is first in
tab order and moves focus to `main`. Fragment links cannot target an id inside a shadow root,
so the skip link is handled with a click listener.

Gaps, per docs/features/_conventions.md's "say so inline" rule: `--main-width` only caps the
main column's max inline size; the open drawer contains focus through `inert` on everything
else rather than a keydown Tab trap, which lets Tab reach the browser chrome (equivalent for
assistive tech).

internal `bx-popup` (docs/features/core/popover.md). Unlike `bx-tooltip` its content can be

tree than the popup body inside this shadow root, so the ID reference cannot resolve.

native Popover API path is not used (only the `bx-popup` positioning path, the same
one-code-path-everywhere reasoning as `bx-popup` itself); `label` and the `anchor` slot are

slot); the `sheet-narrow` bottom-sheet behavior (§5) is not implemented.

declarations.name: BxPopup
declarations.description:
`<bx-popup>` — low-level positioning primitive (anchor, flip, shift, size, arrow) used by
dropdown, select, tooltip, popover.

FR-POPUP-01 implements the Floating-UI-style JS computation path only: `getBoundingClientRect`
already returns viewport coordinates regardless of shadow-root nesting or transformed ancestors
(FR-POPUP-03), so positioning off it is correct in both cases without extra work. The native CSS
Anchor Positioning fast path the spec also allows is not implemented — browser support is not
yet broad enough to be the primary path, and shipping only the JS path keeps this component's
behavior identical everywhere rather than branching per browser — noted here per
docs/features/_conventions.md's "say so inline" rule for partially-implemented FRs (see
`bx-scroller` for the same pattern). `strategy="absolute"` adds `scrollX`/`scrollY` to
viewport-relative coordinates, which assumes the popup's containing block is the initial
containing block (no transformed ancestor between the popup and the document) — `strategy="fixed"`
has no such assumption and is the more robust choice when that isn't guaranteed.

The `anchor` slot fallback (used when the `anchor` property/attribute is unset) has a real
layout limitation worth knowing before reaching for it: `reposition()` makes the *host itself*
`position: absolute`/`fixed` (not an internal wrapper), so anything slotted into `anchor` is
inside that same moving box and gets dragged along with the popup instead of staying at its
original document position — visually, the "anchor" ends up glued above the popup content
rather than acting as a separate, fixed trigger. Every consumer in this package (`bx-tooltip`,
`bx-dialog`'s reuse of `bx-button`, `bx-color-picker`) sidesteps this by always resolving a real
external element themselves and passing it through the `anchor` *property*, which has none of
this problem — prefer that over the slot fallback. Restructuring `reposition()` to position an
inner wrapper instead of the host would fix this properly, but changes this component's public
geometry contract (`popup.getBoundingClientRect()` is relied on directly, including by this
component's own tests) enough that it's being left as a known gap rather than risked here.

declarations.description:
`<bx-progress-bar>` — linear progress indicator, determinate or indeterminate.

`value` and the accessible `label` attribute are independent of the default slot: the slot is
an overlay label rendered on top of the track (e.g. "42%"), hidden once the track's container
is narrower than ~8 fluid units (docs/features/core/progress-bar.md §5), while `label` always
reaches assistive tech via `aria-label` regardless of width.

declarations.name: BxProgressRing
declarations.description:
`<bx-progress-ring>` — circular progress indicator with a centered label.

The filled arc is pure `stroke-dashoffset` math off `value`; there is no JS layout read at
render time (docs/features/core/progress-ring.md FR-PROGRESS-RING-01). `label` is an
accessible label surfaced via `aria-label`; the default slot is the visual text centered
inside the ring — the two are independent, same split as `bx-progress-bar`.

declarations.name: BxRadioGroup
declarations.description:
`<bx-radio-group>` — owns a set of slotted `bx-radio` children: single value, validation, and
`label`/`hint` chrome, form-associated via `ElementInternals` (docs/features/core/radio-group.md).

Mutual exclusion and arrow-key roving tabindex already work without this element — `bx-radio`
self-coordinates by `name` across any connected peers (see that component's own doc comment).
This element adds what a bare `name` grouping can't: it assigns `name` to its slotted children
so the caller doesn't repeat it on every `bx-radio`, cascades `disabled` downward, tracks the
committed `value` from the children's bubbling `input`/`change` events (already `composed`, so
a plain `addEventListener` on the host sees them without any re-dispatch), and is itself the
form-participant (FR-RADIO-GROUP-01) — child radios opt out of their own form participation
while inside a group (see `bx-radio`'s `#syncFormState`) so `FormData` gets one entry, not one
per radio. Home/End (FR-RADIO-GROUP-04) is handled here rather than in `bx-radio`: arrow-key
movement is peer-to-peer and already lives there, but Home/End needs "first/last member of
*this* group", which only the group knows about; `bx-radio`'s own keydown handler ignores those
keys and lets them bubble here.

declarations.name: BxRadio
declarations.description:
`<bx-radio>` — single option within a radio group, form-associated via `ElementInternals`.

Mutual exclusion and roving tabindex are keyed by `name` across all connected instances (see the
`groups` map above), the same peer-coordination approach `bx-details` uses for `name`-grouped
accordions. `name` and `checked` are not in the spec's own properties table
(docs/features/core/radio.md §2) but are required for the element to be usable at all before
`bx-radio-group` exists — see that spec's §10 "confirm final property names during
implementation", and `bx-details`'s `lazy` attribute for the same kind of gap.

`:host` deliberately has no `container-type` — a radio doesn't use `@container` for anything,
and, as a flex item inside a `flex-direction: column` group (`bx-radio-group`'s own layout, or
a consumer's), `container-type: inline-size` measurably changed the host's own block-size by
about 1px depending on `checked` (the checked-icon's presence changing containment's
remembered-size bookkeeping), which read as the whole group visibly shifting by a pixel on
every selection change. Removed for exactly that reason — don't re-add it without a real
`@container` query to justify it.

declarations.name: BxRating
declarations.description:
`<bx-rating>` — star-style rating input/display with fractional precision, form-associated via
`ElementInternals`.

FR-RATING-04's hover preview is a single `clip-path` on one `.fill` overlay (the fully "on"
symbols drawn on top of the always-visible dim `.track` row underneath), not one clip per
symbol — so hovering only ever repaints that one clip boundary, never touches the `max` symbol
nodes themselves, and the pointer handler writes `--bx-rating-fill` straight to the overlay's
`style` (bypassing `requestUpdate`) so a fast mouse sweep doesn't schedule a render per pixel.
FR-RATING-05 (RTL fills right-to-left) falls out of the same technique: the clip inset flips
side under `:host(:dir(rtl))` instead of any per-symbol position math.

`name` is not in the spec's own properties table (docs/features/core/rating.md §2) but is
required for `FormData` to pick the control up at all — the platform keys a form-associated
custom element's submitted entry off its `name` content attribute, the same gap noted on
`bx-radio` and `bx-details`'s `lazy`; see that spec's §10 "confirm final property names during
implementation".

declarations.name: BxRelativeTime
declarations.description:
`<bx-relative-time>` — self-updating relative timestamp ("3 minutes ago") formatted via
`Intl.RelativeTimeFormat`.

Every instance keeps itself current: by default each schedules its own `setTimeout` at an
interval adapted to the displayed unit (every second while reading in seconds, every day once
it reads in months). Setting `sync` opts an instance into the shared page-wide ticker instead
(FR-RELATIVE-TIME-01) — useful for a list of many timestamps, where one coalesced timer beats
dozens of independent ones. Both paths pause while the tab is hidden and catch up immediately on
return (FR-RELATIVE-TIME-02, via the `visibilitychange` listener in  and this
class's own `#onVisibility`).

declarations.name: BxResizeObserver
declarations.description:
`<bx-resize-observer>` — declaratively observes its own box size, firing `bx-resize` on change.

Wraps the page-wide shared `ResizeObserver` (`internal/shared-observers.ts`,
FR-RESIZE-OBSERVER-02) rather than creating its own, and coalesces the native callback's
delivery to one `requestAnimationFrame` per instance (FR-RESIZE-OBSERVER-01) so listeners that
themselves trigger layout (common with resize-driven code) run outside the observer's own
callback turn, avoiding "ResizeObserver loop" warnings.

events.description: The observed box size changed. `detail: { entries: ResizeObserverEntry[] }`.

declarations.name: BxScroller
declarations.description:
`<bx-scroller>` — scroll region with edge shadows and keyboard access.

The scrollable element lives in the shadow root (`part="content"`) and is the thing that
actually receives focus/`tabindex`, not the host — a focused `overflow: auto` element already
scrolls with arrow/space/page keys natively, so no custom key handling is needed
(FR-SCROLLER-02). It only becomes a tab stop once its content actually overflows.

Edge shadows are driven by a passive, rAF-throttled `scroll` listener plus a shared
`ResizeObserver` (docs/features/core/scroller.md FR-SCROLLER-01's documented JS fallback path).
The scroll-driven-animation alternative the spec also allows is not implemented: browser
support for timelining an animation off a shadow-DOM-internal scrollport is still inconsistent
enough that the JS path is the more reliable default — noted here per
docs/features/_conventions.md's "say so inline" rule for partially-implemented FRs.

`role="region"` is only added once the content is scrollable *and* the host has an accessible
name (`aria-label`/`aria-labelledby`) — an unnamed region is worse for assistive tech than no
region at all, so the keyboard tab stop still applies without one, but the landmark role waits
for a name (docs/features/core/scroller.md §6).

declarations.name: BxSelect
declarations.description:
`<bx-select>` — single or multiple choice with a searchable, virtualized listbox and
removable-badge display for selections (docs/features/core/select.md).

**ARIA.** The focus target is a native `<input role="combobox">` in the shadow root (readonly
unless `searchable`), so the browser supplies caret, IME and selection behavior. DOM focus
never leaves it: the highlighted option is exposed through `aria-activedescendant`, which is
what keeps FR-SELECT-06 true when option nodes are recycled by the virtualizer. The ID
reference crosses from this shadow root to a slotted light-DOM `bx-option`, so it is set through
the `ariaActiveDescendantElement` element-reflection property (`bx-option` carries `role="option"`
on its host for exactly that reason). Browsers without element reflection fall back to the
`aria-activedescendant` attribute, which only resolves for options rendered in this shadow root
(data-driven / virtual lists).

**Options.** Either slotted `bx-option`/`bx-divider` children or the `options` data array
(`{ value, label?, disabled?, group? }`; required for 10k+ items since it creates no elements).
Both are normalized into one row model, so search, typeahead, selected-label lookup and
`aria-setsize`/`aria-posinset` always run over the *full* data set, never the rendered window.
When the list is windowed (`virtual`, or `auto` at 200+ options) the slotted options are used as
data only and rows are rendered by this component, so a slotted option's `start`/`end` slot
content is not shown in that mode. Slotted `label`/`value` are read from attributes and text;
changing them through properties alone is not observed.

**Deviations / gaps, per docs/features/_conventions.md's "say so inline" rule:**
- FR-SELECT-04's "index built off-thread" is not implemented: filtering and typeahead run on the
  main thread over lazily-built, pre-lowered search keys (a few ms at 100k rows).
- `readonly` and `open` are added (neither is in the spec's property table). `form` is the
  native `form` content attribute, which the browser already honors for form-associated
  elements, so it is not re-declared as a property.
- `value` is a `string` when single and a `string[]` when `multiple`; as an attribute, multiple
  values are whitespace-separated. A multiple select submits one `FormData` entry per value.
- `bx-search` is emitted only when `remote` is set (it replaces local filtering); `detail.signal`
  is aborted when a newer query supersedes it (FR-SELECT-07).
- Group headers are visual rows (`role="presentation"`), not `role="group"`: a flat, windowed
  list cannot nest options inside a group element.
- `max-options-visible="auto"` fits tags to the measured width using the shared
  `ResizeObserver`.
- `required` has no visual asterisk of its own; style it from the label.

declarations.name: BxSkeleton
declarations.description:
`<bx-skeleton>` — placeholder shimmer while content loads.

Shape is composed with plain CSS on the host (width/height, `--bx-skeleton-border-radius`) —
there is no `shape` property; set `border-radius: 50%` for a circle avatar placeholder, a
fixed `block-size` for a block, or leave the 1-line-height default alone for a text line.
The skeleton itself is `aria-hidden` since it carries no content; a container holding one or
more skeletons should set `aria-busy="true"` (docs/features/core/skeleton.md §6).

The shimmer pauses while off-screen, via the shared `IntersectionObserver`
(docs/features/_conventions.md §9), and under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

declarations.name: BxSlider
declarations.description:
`<bx-slider>` — single or range slider, form-associated via `ElementInternals`.

Single mode reports through `value`/`name` like a native `<input type="range">`. Range mode
(FR-SLIDER-05: thumbs cannot cross) reports both ends as a `FormData` pair under `${name}-min`/
`${name}-max` — `ElementInternals.setFormValue` accepts a `FormData` for exactly this
multi-value case, so no extra hidden inputs are needed (docs/features/core/slider.md §10:
"confirm final property names during implementation" — the `-min`/`-max` suffix is this
component's answer for now).

A slider's value is never "missing" the way a checkbox or text field can be — there's always a
number in range — so `required` has no native meaning here either (`<input type="range">` does
not support it); validity stays permanently valid, matching that platform gap intentionally
rather than inventing a made-up failure mode.

declarations.name: BxSpinner
declarations.description:
`<bx-spinner>` — indeterminate loading spinner.

Sized in `1em` by default so it tracks the surrounding text's `font-size`; set `font-size` on
the host (or an ancestor) to scale it instead of a dedicated size property. Has no `value` —
for determinate progress use `bx-progress-ring` or `bx-progress-bar`.

Consumers must supply an `aria-label` (or `aria-labelledby`) describing what is loading; the
host exposes `role="progressbar"` with no `aria-valuenow` so assistive tech announces it as
busy rather than reading a stale percentage.

declarations.name: BxSwitch
declarations.description:
`<bx-switch>` — on/off toggle, form-associated via `ElementInternals`.

Shares its focus/click delegation approach with `bx-checkbox` (`delegatesFocus` + a host-level
listener) — see that component's doc comment for why. `role="switch"` control size and the
`--bx-switch-*` custom properties are on the control alone.

declarations.name: BxTabGroup
declarations.description:
`<bx-tab-group>` — tabbed interface owning a `nav`-slotted set of `bx-tab` and a default-slotted
set of `bx-tab-panel` (docs/features/core/tab-group.md).

Wires the two: matches each tab's `panel` to a panel's `name`, drives `active` on both from this
element's own `active`, and drives roving tabindex through `bx-tab`'s `tab-stop` property (APG
tabs pattern — only the active tab, or the most recently focused one once focus has moved off
it, is a tab stop). `aria-controls`/`aria-labelledby` cross the tab's and panel's separate shadow
roots via `bx-tab`'s `controlsElement`/`tabElement` and the platform's `ariaLabelledByElements`
(`bx-tab`'s own doc comment explains why a plain ID-string attribute can't do this), not a plain
attribute string.

FR-TAB-GROUP-02 ("inactive panels are not rendered until first shown when `lazy`") is not
implemented: panels are ordinary slotted light-DOM content, so genuine deferred instantiation
would need a `<template>`-based content model this spec doesn't define yet. `bx-tab-panel`'s
existing `hidden` attribute (docs/features/core/tab-panel.md FR-TAB-PANEL-01) already keeps an
inactive panel out of layout/paint/the accessibility tree, which covers the FR's practical
performance intent; a `lazy` attribute is deliberately omitted rather than added as a no-op, per
docs/features/_conventions.md's "say so inline instead of leaving it silent" rule for genuine
gaps.

Overflow scrolling (FR-TAB-GROUP-01) reuses the shared `ResizeObserver` pool, the same
measure-on-resize-and-scroll approach as `bx-scroller`.

declarations.name: BxTabPanel
declarations.description:
`<bx-tab-panel>` — content for a tab.

`role="tabpanel"` lives on the host itself (the `bx-divider`/`bx-carousel-item` host-attribute
pattern) since there's no interactive shadow content to hang it on. `aria-labelledby` — "labelled
by tab" (docs/features/core/tab-panel.md §6) — is left for the consumer/future `bx-tab-group` to
set directly as a plain attribute on the host, the same way any ARIA-reflecting custom element
accepts it; nothing here needs to compute or own that value.

FR-TAB-PANEL-01: inactive panels use the `hidden` content attribute rather than a CSS display
trick, so they're fully removed from the accessibility tree (and from tab order) rather than
merely invisible.

declarations.name: BxTab
declarations.description:
`<bx-tab>` — a tab button.

`panel` (docs/features/core/tab.md §2's "Panel name") is *not* rendered as a plain
`aria-controls="<panel>"` string attribute: `role="tab"` lives on an element inside this
component's own shadow root, and a plain IDREF attribute only resolves within the referencing
element's own root — it can never reach a `bx-tab-panel` host out in the light DOM, and shipping
one anyway is an `aria-valid-attr-value` violation waiting to happen (a real one surfaced in
`bx-tab-group`'s own tests). `controlsElement` below sets the real relationship across that
boundary via `ariaControlsElements` (the cross-root-capable ARIA element-reference reflection),
which `bx-tab-group` drives; standalone, nothing sets it, so a lone tab simply has no
`aria-controls` relationship, which is correct — there is nothing to control.

Roving tabindex across a set of tabs (only the active or, once one has focus, the most recently
focused tab is a tab stop) is driven through `tab-stop` below, which `bx-tab-group` sets per
APG's roving-tabindex pattern; standalone, a tab defaults to `tab-stop`, so it's still
independently keyboard-testable without a group.

members.description:
Roving-tabindex hook, driven by `bx-tab-group`; not in the spec's own properties table (see

events.description: The close button (present when `closable`) was activated, by click or by Backspace/Delete on the focused tab. Not fired when `disabled`.

cssParts.description: The close glyph, present when `closable` (not in the spec's own CSS parts table — added the same way `bx-badge`'s `remove-button` part exists for its own removable-chip case). It's a plain `aria-hidden` span, not its own focusable control: a focusable descendant of a `role="tab"` element is an ARIA nested-interactive violation (axe: nested-interactive) no matter its `tabindex`, since `tab` is itself an interactive widget role. Mouse users click it directly; keyboard users close via Backspace/Delete on the tab itself, the same pattern `bx-badge`'s removable chip uses for the same reason.

declarations.name: BxTextarea
declarations.description:
`<bx-textarea>` — multi-line text field, form-associated via `ElementInternals`, wrapping a
real native `<textarea>` in its shadow root (docs/features/core/textarea.md).

Shares `bx-input`'s label/hint chrome and validity-forwarding approach verbatim (that
component's own doc comment): the native `<textarea>`'s own `ValidityState` is forwarded to
`internals.setValidity` rather than reimplemented.

FR-TEXTAREA-04's auto-resize (`resize="auto"`) prefers `field-sizing: content` (CSS,
detected once via `CSS.supports` at module load — cheap, and the answer can't change at
runtime) and only runs the rAF-batched `scrollHeight` measurement fallback when that isn't
supported, the same "modern CSS path with a JS fallback, pick one at runtime" precedent
`bx-scroller`'s edge shadows and `bx-popup`'s positioning already set.

FR-TEXTAREA-05 ("handles ≥1 MB values without freezing: count computed lazily") is naturally
satisfied by `value.length`, an O(1) string-length read regardless of content size — the actual
cost this FR guards against is a *counter render* on every keystroke for a huge value, which is
why the visible counter and the `aria-live` announcement are two separate elements: the visible
one updates every keystroke (cheap), the announced one only updates at `ANNOUNCE_THRESHOLDS`.

declarations.name: BxTooltip
declarations.description:
`<bx-tooltip>` — short hover/focus hint anchored to any element, positioned by an internal
`bx-popup` (docs/features/core/tooltip.md).

Anchoring is `for` (an id, resolved with a plain `document.getElementById` rather than
`bx-popup`'s own root-scoped resolution — the spec's own "works across shadow roots" note for
`for`, docs/features/core/tooltip.md §2) or, when `for` is unset, a slotted anchor element. The
spec's own slots table lists only `(default)` (the tooltip's body content, forwarded to the
inner `bx-popup`'s default slot) — no `anchor` slot — but "anchored to any element via for OR
slot" (§1) needs one; added the same way `bx-tree-item`'s `children` slot fills an analogous gap
in that component's own spec.

FR-TOOLTIP-01's "hover-to-persist over tooltip body" (WCAG 1.4.13) reuses `bx-popup`'s own
`hover-bridge` (an invisible bridge over the anchor-to-popup gap) rather than reimplementing it,
plus this element's own `mouseenter`/`mouseleave` on the popup body itself.

FR-TOOLTIP-03 ("works on disabled controls via wrapper detection") is not implemented for
arbitrary native-`disabled` elements: a genuinely `disabled` native control suppresses pointer
events in a way no listener placement fully works around cross-browser without a dedicated
non-interactive wrapper element this spec doesn't define. It already works for every control in
this package, though — `bx-button`'s own doc comment explains why `disabled` there is never the
inner native `disabled` attribute (so hover/focus keep firing) precisely so a `bx-tooltip`
anchored to a disabled `bx-button` works without any extra effort. Flagged here per
docs/features/_conventions.md's "say so inline" rule rather than silently assumed to cover
plain native elements too.

§6's "anchor gets aria-describedby" is also not implemented, and this one needed hands-on
checking rather than assuming either way: `bx-tab-group` gets a cross-shadow-root ARIA
relationship working with `ariaControlsElements`/`ariaLabelledByElements` (that component's own
doc comment) because the *referencing* element there is the shadow-internal one, pointing out to
a light-DOM target. Here the direction is reversed — the anchor (light DOM, often not even a
Bixant component) would need to reference *into* this element's own shadow root (the popup body)
— and verified against this package's actual pinned Chromium, `ariaDescribedByElements` set that
way reads back as an empty list; the reflected `aria-describedby` content attribute it also
writes comes back empty too. Shadow DOM encapsulation seems to allow a shadow tree reaching out
to reference public light-DOM elements, not the reverse. Left unimplemented rather than shipping
something that silently sets a property with no effect, per docs/features/_conventions.md's "say
so inline" rule.

declarations.name: BxTreeItem
declarations.description:
`<bx-tree-item>` — a node in `bx-tree`, with lazy children.

ARIA tree semantics (`role="treeitem"`, `aria-level`, `aria-selected`, roving tabindex across
siblings) are explicitly the future `bx-tree` parent's job per docs/features/core/tree-item.md
§6, so none of that is set here. What *is* implemented standalone, so the item is independently
usable and keyboard-testable before that parent exists: the expand/collapse button and the
optional selection checkbox are each real, individually focusable controls, and indentation is
computed from actual DOM nesting depth (counting `bx-tree-item` ancestors at connect time) rather
than waiting on a level number a parent would otherwise have to compute and push down.

Nested items go in a `children` slot — not in the spec's own slots table, added the same way
`bx-breadcrumb-item`'s `current` property was: the default slot is the label only, and a
separate slot is what lets the `children` CSS part wrap and hide exactly that content without
text-sniffing the default slot's assigned nodes.

FR-TREE-ITEM-01's lazy loading is a three-event contract mirroring the shape (not the tag name)
of Shoelace's `sl-tree-item`: expanding a `lazy` item that hasn't loaded yet sets `loading` and
fires cancelable `bx-lazy-load`; the consumer does its async work, populates the `children` slot,
and sets `loading = false` (also setting `lazy-error` first if it failed) — this component reacts
to that transition by firing `bx-lazy-change` and, on success, actually expanding. A failed load
leaves `hasLoadedOnce` false, so clicking expand again simply retries.

`indeterminate` and the checkbox's own `change` event exist for `bx-tree`'s tri-state parent
selection (FR-TREE-01): the expand-button and checkbox clicks both already `stopPropagation()`
on the originating `click`, so a bubbled `change` — dispatched separately, unaffected by that —
is `bx-tree`'s only signal that the checkbox (as opposed to the row, which it delegates itself)
changed this item's `selected`.

declarations.name: BxTree
declarations.description:
`<bx-tree>` — hierarchical tree owning a default-slotted, arbitrarily nested set of
`bx-tree-item` (docs/features/core/tree.md).

Supplies everything `bx-tree-item`'s own doc comment defers: `role="tree"` on the shadow
wrapper (slot-flattening already makes light-DOM, and nested-shadow-root, `bx-tree-item`s
register as its accessible descendants — the same mechanism `bx-tab-group`'s `role="tablist"`
relies on), `role="treeitem"`/`aria-level`/`aria-setsize`/`aria-posinset`/`aria-expanded`/
`aria-selected` on each item's host, and roving tabindex + full keyboard navigation
(FR-TREE-02: arrow keys, Home/End, typeahead, `*` to expand siblings).

Roving tabindex needs `bx-tree-item`'s `roving` property: standalone, its expand-button and
checkbox are each their own tab stop (that component's own doc comment); once wrapped here,
APG's tree pattern wants exactly one tab stop per visible row, on the row itself, not its
controls — `roving` (set on every item below) tells `bx-tree-item` to stop making those two
controls independently focusable, and this element puts the host's own `tabIndex` on whichever
item is current instead. Expanding/collapsing still routes through `bx-tree-item`'s own private
lazy-load state machine (`bx-lazy-load`/`bx-lazy-change`) rather than reimplementing it — this
element simulates a click on that item's own expand button (`shadowRoot.querySelector`) instead
of touching `expanded` directly, the one place this component reaches into a child's shadow
root rather than using a property it exposes.

The checkbox-tree tri-state pattern (FR-TREE-01) here is a deliberate deviation from APG's own
"checkbox tree" pattern, which expects `aria-checked` on the treeitem itself with *no* separate
focusable checkbox control — `bx-tree-item` already ships a real nested `role="checkbox"`
(accepted at the Tier 1 level for standalone usability, docs/features/IMPLEMENTATION.md), so
this element cascades selection through it rather than replacing it. Flagged here per
docs/features/_conventions.md's "say so inline" rule rather than silently assumed compliant.

FR-TREE-03's node-count warning fires once per instance the same way `bx-format-date`/
`bx-relative-time` warn on bad input: a plain `console.warn`, no dev/prod build-mode gate (this
package has no such infra yet).

declarations.name: BxZoomableFrame
declarations.description:
`<bx-zoomable-frame>` — iframe with zoom controls. Not form-associated.

FR-ZOOMABLE-FRAME-01: the iframe's own box is sized to `100% / zoom` and then scaled back up by
`zoom` with `transform-origin: top left`, so the *visible* footprint the host occupies never
changes — only what's rendered inside appears to zoom. FR-ZOOMABLE-FRAME-02: `sandbox` defaults
to the empty string (the platform's most restrictive combination — no scripts, no same-origin,
no forms, no popups) rather than omitting the attribute (which would mean *unsandboxed*);
callers opt back into specific capabilities explicitly via the `sandbox` attribute.

`label` is not in the spec's own properties table (docs/features/core/zoomable-frame.md §2) but
is required to satisfy that same spec's §6 "iframe requires `title`" — see `bx-radio`/
`bx-rating`'s `name` for the same kind of gap, and that spec's §10 "confirm final property names
during implementation".
